name: Admin operates the live operations dashboard
description: Verifies every primary administrator dashboard tile opens a usable operational surface instead of acting as decorative UI.
steps: Sign in with an approved Nightjar administrator email
Open Listener People, Creator People and Administrator People
Open Creator Approvals and inspect the queue
Open Revenue, Subscriptions and Listening Economics
expected: Each administrator tile opens a functional view or protected operational destination, and no tile relies on a notification-only placeholder.

name: Admin previews every account role without changing administrator access
description: Verifies the administrator can inspect all role-facing product surfaces while the real backend role remains Administrator.
steps: Open Admin as an approved administrator
Preview Writer and create a local draft in preview
Preview Editor and inspect the editorial queue
expected: Each role preview renders its own surface, the preview banner identifies the real Administrator role, and returning to Admin restores the operational dashboard.

name: Daily spotlights rotate fairly in a fixed five-place order
description: Verifies the discovery page presents separate creator and writer spotlight tiles using a deterministic one-day rotation rather than random reshuffling.
steps: Confirm both show a one-day spotlight window and a new edition or script
Return on a later day and confirm the rotation advances to the next fixed position
expected: Exactly one creator and one writer occupy the daily spotlight, each remains featured for the full day, and the sequence advances in the same fixed order across the five-place cycle.

name: Creator sees transparent listening economics and protected script access
description: Verifies the Creator surface presents listening and revenue attribution while keeping manuscript copy and export permissions separate.
expected: Creator Studio shows listening and attribution information, and the protected script remains readable with copy and export off.

name: Use the Protection Centre
description: Verifies a signed-in user can submit a protection report and inspect supporting evidence without exposing clipboard contents.
expected: Nightjar creates a case ID, the case appears in My Cases, and evidence records are available as supporting signals.

name: Normal account cannot access administrator overview
description: Verifies administrator-only operational data is not available to a normal listener or creator account.
steps: Sign in with a normal Nightjar account
Open the account as a Listener
expected: The normal account remains outside the administrator area and cannot access administrator-only People, approvals or subscription data.

name: Every account can build a personalised Nightjar profile
description: Verifies the shared identity layer is available independently of account role.
steps: Set a chosen name and unique @handle
Add favourite tags, tropes and categories
expected: The personalised profile persists and remains separate from the account's permission role.

name: Protected script activity creates an all-owner security alert
description: Verifies qualifying protected-content activity becomes a retained security alert addressed to all three Nightjar owners.
steps: Open a protected script with an approved account
Generate qualifying high-volume protected-content events in a test environment
expected: A retained security alert identifies the account/session/script signals and records both owner recipients; an administrator can suspend the account, which revokes active reader sessions.

name: People directory represents every Nightjar account role
description: Verifies administrator People is a real five-role directory rather than an administrator-only/partial list.
expected: All five roles have dedicated directory surfaces, counts come from real account data except the three configured owner administrators, and no fake account records are created.

name: Administrator allowlist includes all Nightjar owners
description: Verifies every configured Nightjar owner is represented as an administrator and that owner-only security controls use the same allowlist.
steps: Sign in with each approved Nightjar owner email in a test environment
expected: All three approved owner accounts are represented as active Administrators, and security alerts are addressed to the same three configured owners.
